Find PWM motif hits in genomic intervals

Source: R/pwm-hits.R
gintervals.pwm_hits.Rd

Returns, for each interval, the motif windows that reach score.thresh: exactly the windows a pwm.count virtual track with the same parameters counts over that interval, as intervals with their strand and score. It replaces running gscreen over a 1 bp iterator.

Usage

gintervals.pwm_hits(
  intervals = NULL,
  pssm = NULL,
  score.thresh = NULL,
  bidirect = TRUE,
  strand = 1L,
  prior = 0.01,
  extend = TRUE
)

Arguments

intervals

genomic intervals to scan

pssm

numeric matrix or data frame with columns A, C, G, T; each row holds the probabilities or counts of the four bases at one motif position.

score.thresh

single number; windows scoring at or above it are hits.

bidirect

logical; if TRUE (default) both strands are scanned.

strand

1 or -1: the strand scanned when bidirect = FALSE.

prior

numeric; pseudocount added to the frequencies (default 0.01).

extend

logical; if TRUE (default) a window anchored near an interval's end may read bases past it.

Value

An intervals data frame with columns chrom, start, end (the window), strand, score and intervalID (the row of intervals the window is anchored in), sorted by intervalID and start; NULL when nothing passes. Overlapping input intervals report a window once per interval it is anchored in.

Details

A window is anchored at its first (leftmost) base, which must lie in the interval; with extend = TRUE it may run up to w - 1 bases past the interval's end (w being the motif length), as the PWM virtual tracks do. Scores are natural-log likelihoods including the prior, computed as the pwm virtual tracks compute them (in single precision), and a window holding N or any other non-ACGT base is not scored. Windows that cannot reach the threshold are skipped without being scored, which makes a strict threshold fast; the hits are the same as scoring every window.

Strand: under bidirect = TRUE a window is one hit, whose score is the log-sum-exp of its forward and reverse-complement scores (the value pwm.count thresholds), and whose strand is the strand that scores higher on its own (1 on a tie), as pwm.max.pos names it. Under bidirect = FALSE only the strand named by strand is read and strand is that strand. A strand column of intervals is ignored, as by the virtual tracks. start and end are genomic coordinates of the window whatever the strand.

See also

gseq.pwm_hits, gvtrack.create for the pwm.count virtual track.

Examples


gdb.init_examples()
pssm <- matrix(
    c(
        0.7, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1,
        0.1, 0.7, 0.1, 0.1,
        0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.1,
        0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7
    ),
    ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "C", "G", "T"))
)
intervs <- gintervals(1, 0, 10000)
hits <- gintervals.pwm_hits(intervs, pssm, score.thresh = -3)
head(hits)
#>   chrom start end strand     score intervalID
#> 1  chr1   176 180      1 -2.698482          1
#> 2  chr1   504 508      1 -2.698482          1
#> 3  chr1   561 565      1 -2.698482          1
#> 4  chr1   607 611      1 -2.698482          1
#> 5  chr1   664 668      1 -2.698482          1
#> 6  chr1   674 678      1 -2.698482          1

# the windows pwm.count counts
gvtrack.create("motif_count", NULL, "pwm.count", pssm = pssm, score.thresh = -3)
gextract("motif_count", intervs, iterator = intervs)
#>   chrom start   end motif_count intervalID
#> 1  chr1     0 10000         269          1
